archetype.name: Dual-Threat (designed-run)
archetype.definition: A quarterback whose legs are a planned part of the offense, with called runs and a rookie-year rushing total that ranked third among qualifiers, paired with a passing game that wins short and over the middle rather than downfield.

report.headline: One brilliant game against a bad defense, then an injury: verdict deferred.
report.take:
Jaxson Dart's 2026 season is essentially one game. He played every snap of a Week 1 win over Dallas, played 12% of the snaps in Week 2 at the Rams, and has since gone to injured reserve. Jameis Winston started Weeks 3 and 4, and the depth chart now lists Dart fourth. So the headline numbers come from a 29-attempt day: his 0.578 EPA per dropback ranks first of 42, and he has the best completion rate and no interceptions. That day came against a Dallas defense that now ranks 31st. It is a real performance, but it is a small sample against a soft opponent.

What produced that game is worth noting, because some of it fits who he was as a rookie. He was a Dual-Threat in 2025, with 487 rushing yards ranking third among 65 quarterbacks, and the Week 1 designed runs (six of them, all successful, 8.2 yards a carry) are the same weapon. The passing was different. His rookie CPOE was below average (36th of 65). Against Dallas he was surgical underneath and in the intermediate zone: 13 of 14 on short throws and +1.17 EPA per play on 10-to-19-yard attempts, plus a perfect 7-for-7 with three touchdowns in the red zone. Isaiah Likely, at 1.36 EPA per target, and Malik Nabers took most of the looks.

The numbers hide plenty. The red zone and third down (88.9% conversions) are seven- and nine-play samples that will not hold. He was 0-for-3 on deep throws. One habit followed him from his rookie year: his pressure-to-sack rate was 45th of 64 in 2025 and is 26th of 32 now. He holds the ball looking for something, and that carries more risk behind a Giants line whose offensive hit rate is 30th. The scheme matters too. John Harbaugh's offense passes 10 points less than situation predicts, 31st in the league, which caps his passing volume even when he is healthy.

Where it goes depends entirely on when he gets off IR and whether he gets the job back. The dossier gives no injury type or return date, and he is listed as QB4. Until he is back, there is nothing to project week to week. When he returns, expect something closer to his rookie profile, with real rushing value and modest passing volume, than to the Week 1 outlier.

strengths.title: Designed runs are a real weapon
strengths.body: His rushing is the most durable part of his profile. He finished third among 65 quarterbacks in rushing yards as a rookie, and Week 1's called runs were all successful, a third of them explosive. Because it shows up across both seasons, this is the part to bank on whenever he plays.

strengths.title: Efficient underneath and intermediate passing
strengths.body: Against Dallas he completed nearly everything inside 20 yards. That came with a +17 CPOE on short throws and over 1.1 EPA per play in the intermediate zone, mostly to Likely and Nabers. The accuracy is far above his rookie CPOE, so treat it as a positive sign rather than a new baseline: it came on 25 attempts against the league's 31st-ranked defense.

strengths.title: Clean ball security so far
strengths.body: He has no interceptions and no lost fumbles this year, and his bad-throw rate dropped from 15% as a rookie to 11.8%. He did log one turnover-worthy fumble, so this is a modest improvement, not a solved problem.

concerns.title: On IR and buried on the depth chart
concerns.body: He played 12% of the snaps in Week 2, did not practice in Week 3, and is now on injured reserve and listed as QB4. Winston has made the last two starts. No return date or injury detail is given, so even a return to health doesn't guarantee the job is waiting for him.

concerns.title: Pressure turns into sacks
concerns.body: A third of his pressures have ended in sacks, ranking 26th of 32. That matches a rookie season where he ranked 45th of 64. It is a lasting trait of a quarterback who extends and holds the ball, not a fluke. Behind a line allowing hits at the league's third-worst rate, it is a lasting drag on his efficiency and his health.

concerns.title: Week 1 rates will regress
concerns.body: Perfect red-zone passing and an 88.9% third-down conversion rate on 7 and 9 plays are not repeatable. Neither is EPA per dropback leading the league off one start. He was also 0-for-3 deep, and the run-heavy scheme caps volume, so even a healthy Dart projects nearer his rookie efficiency.

trend.note: A 26.6-point Week 1 against Dallas was followed by 12% of the snaps at the Rams and then injured reserve. The drop reflects his availability, not his play.

nextGame.headline: On IR: a soft Washington secondary he likely won't face
nextGame.body:
On paper this is a good matchup for his position. Washington allows 22.5 PPR points a game to quarterbacks (30th) and three touchdowns a game (31st). Its defense is tough on short throws (5th) but leaks badly deep (26th in deep EPA). That last point matters less for Dart, who went 0-for-3 deep and wins underneath. It also matches how the Giants defense plays, which limits explosive passes.

Availability decides everything. Dart is on injured reserve and listed fourth on the depth chart, and Winston started Weeks 3 and 4, so Dart should not be expected to play. On Washington's side, safety Nick Cross (99% of snaps) is out and safety Jeremy Reaves is questionable. That thins a secondary already struggling deep, which helps whoever starts for New York. Jayden Daniels is listed out with a dislocated elbow but the team is aiming for him to start, with Mariota doubtful behind him. Terry McLaurin is also out.

keyMatchups.title: Washington's deep-pass leak
keyMatchups.body: Washington gives up over a point of EPA per deep play, 26th in the league. With Cross out, the back end gets thinner. That is a better spot for Winston's aggressive style than for Dart's short game.

keyMatchups.title: Short area is closed off
keyMatchups.body: Washington ranks 5th against short passes, which is exactly where Dart did his best work in Week 1. Even if he were active, his most efficient area would face Washington's best coverage.

keyMatchups.title: Who starts at quarterback for New York
keyMatchups.body: Winston has started the last two games while Dart sits on IR. Any Dart outlook for this week is contingent on a surprise activation, which nothing in the dossier suggests.

nextGame.watch: Whether Dart is designated to return from IR and moves up the depth chart. Until then, Winston is the Giants' quarterback.

restOfSeason.body:
Once he's back, the sustainable part is the rushing: designed runs and scrambles that produced 487 yards as a rookie and 54 in his one full game this year. The passing should settle well below Week 1, likely around his rookie EPA of roughly 0.15 per play rather than 0.58. That means a completion rate in the 60s, not the 70s, and touchdowns at a normal rate rather than 8.8% of attempts. Harbaugh's run-first approach keeps attempts in the high 20s, which caps his yardage ceiling.

The bigger unknowns are timing and role. He's on IR with no listed return date and sits fourth on the depth chart behind a Winston-led offense. The projections below assume he returns as the starter. If Winston plays well enough to keep the job, Dart's rest-of-season value could be close to zero.
swingFactors: IR return date and his health on return
Whether Harbaugh hands the job back over Winston
Pass protection, given the line's 30th-ranked hit rate

bets.reason: Neither offense moves the ball consistently: the Giants rank 26th and Washington 29th in success rate, and the Giants pass the second-least over expectation. Washington is missing McLaurin and has real doubt about Daniels, with Mariota doubtful behind him. The Giants defense ranks 6th in explosive passes allowed and 3rd in deep EPA allowed, limiting the big plays that usually push a total over.

confidence.note: One full game against the 31st-ranked defense, now on IR with no return date and listed QB4.
